Report on filters used on a snpRdata object.

filters.Rd

snpR will automatically track the methods used on a snpRdata object. Using filters on that object will provide details on the the filters used.

Usage

filters(x)

Arguments

x

snpRdata object

Value

Prints easily human readable results to the console and also returns a more machine readable string.

Details

Printed outputs contain the filters used in the order they were applied alongside the filtering stringency and any facets applied over, if applicable. Note that some output formats from format_snps, like the vcf format, will notes on the filters used as well.

Author

William Hemstrom

Examples

# filter the data
x <- filter_snps(stickSNPs, 
                 min_ind = 0.75, 
                 min_loci = 0.75,
                 maf = 0.1,
                 maf_facets = "pop")
#> Adding missing facets...
#> Initializing...
#> Filtering loci. Starting loci: 100 
#> Filtering non-biallelic loci...
#> 	0 bad loci
#> Filtering non_polymorphic loci...
#> 	0 bad loci
#> Filtering loci sequenced in few individuals...
#> 	9 bad loci
#> Filtering low minor allele frequencies by facet.
#> 	6 bad loci
#> 	Ending loci: 85 
#> Filtering individuals. Starting individuals: 100 
#> Filtering out individuals sequenced in few kept loci...
#> Re-calculating and adding facets.
#> 	Ending individuals: 95 
#> Re-filtering loci...
#> Filtering non_polymorphic loci...
#> 	0 bad loci
#> 	Final loci count: 85 

# fetch the filters used
filters(x)
#> Filter: bi-allelic 
#> 
#> Filter: bi-allelic 
#> 
#> Filter: non-polymorphic 
#> 
#> Filter: poorly sequenced loci--min_ind 
#> 	Stringency: 0.75 
#> 	Facet: .base 
#> 
#> Filter: Minor Allele Frequency--maf 
#> 	Stringency: 0.1 
#> 	Facet: pop 
#> 
#> Filter: poorly sequenced individuals--min_loci 
#> 	Stringency: 0.75 
#> 
#> Filter: non-polymorphic 
#> 
#> [1] "bi-allelic;bi-allelic;non-polymorphic;min_ind=0.75,facet=.base;maf=0.1,facet=pop;min_loci=0.75;non-polymorphic"
